title: Senior Enablement Program Manager, Support Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The Technical Solutions (TS) Enablement team empowers Datadog's global post-sales organization—including Support, Customer Success, and Sales Engineering—with the skills, tools, and resources they need to deliver world-class customer outcomes. As a Senior TS Enablement Program Manager supporting Global Support Engineering, you'll own the design and execution of complex, high-visibility enablement programs that drive lasting change across the TS organization. You'll operate with significant autonomy, lead cross-functional initiatives, and serve as a senior voice within the Enablement team—partnering closely with leadership to translate business priorities into measurable enablement impact at scale.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end strategy and execution for complex, global enablement programs—managing multiple concurrent workstreams across regions, functions, and timelines with limited guidance.
  • Lead cross-functional stakeholder relationships with senior partners across StratOps, Product, TS Leadership, and the People Team—negotiating scope, aligning on priorities, and driving accountability without positional authority.
  • Translate business goals and OKRs into multi-quarter program roadmaps; communicate priorities, trade-offs, and progress to leadership with clarity and a clear point of view.
  • Design and implement comprehensive metrics frameworks to measure change adoption and program effectiveness; pull and analyze Salesforce and LMS data to track performance against KPIs; present findings to senior stakeholders and iterate for lasting impact.
  • Build and deliver executive-ready materials that tell a compelling business story—translating complex data, program updates, and regional insights into structured narratives with clear recommendations.
  • Conduct ongoing needs assessments, stakeholder interviews, and pulse checks across TS regions; synthesize qualitative and quantitative feedback to inform program strategy and surface emerging gaps.
  • Design the tools, resources, communications, and training frameworks needed to support TS workflow changes at scale—partnering with Curriculum and Field teams on content development and delivery.
  • Partner with Global Support Engineering leadership to design ramp and enablement programs that account for differences in specialist vs. generalist skill development across the support org.
  • Mentor and develop junior EPM ICs on the team—providing structured feedback on program design and stakeholder management, and raising the quality bar across program work.
  • Identify and implement AI-powered workflows, automations, and process improvements that increase the efficiency, consistency, and scalability of enablement programs—from reporting and data pipelines to content creation and stakeholder communications.
  • Maintain a deep, current understanding of regional needs, TS team performance, and functional priorities to ensure programs remain relevant and impactful across a global audience.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6–8 years of related experience in enablement, program management, change management, or a closely related field—or a Master’s degree with 4+ years.
  • Proven track record leading complex, multi-quarter programs with high visibility—comfortable operating independently and making sound judgment calls with limited oversight.
  • Expert at building and managing senior stakeholder relationships across functions; can drive alignment, navigate competing priorities, and influence outcomes without positional authority.
  • Deeply data-driven—you design measurement frameworks, analyze program and performance data, and build Salesforce and LMS reports to connect enablement programs to field KPIs and business outcomes.
  • Exceptional presentation and communication skills—builds well-structured, visually compelling decks and delivers them confidently to senior and executive audiences with a clear, well-reasoned point of view.
  • Expert in change management and organizational development best practices, with a demonstrated history of driving adoption at scale across global organizations. PROSCI/ADKAR certification (or equivalent) required.
  • Deep understanding of the day-to-day responsibilities, challenges, and workflows of the TS functions you support; recognized as a credible strategic partner, not just a program coordinator.
  • Skilled in program management tools (Asana, Jira) and collaboration platforms (Confluence, Slack, Docebo).
  • Actively applies AI tools (e.g., Claude, agentic workflows) to streamline operations, surface insights, and improve program delivery—and helps others on the team do the same.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on experience in, or working closely alongside, a technical support organization (e.g., prior support engineer, specialist support, or generalist support experience).
  • Expert-level familiarity with instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, Kirkpatrick) and adult learning theory.
  • Experience building or scaling enablement programs in a high-growth or enterprise SaaS environment.
  • Track record of successfully delivering global programs across multiple regions (Americas, EMEA, APJ).
  • Proficient with the Datadog platform and monitoring best practices (e.g., DD Fundamentals certified), with solid working knowledge of the observability industry and the personas your audience serves.

title: Manager, Internal Product Analytics
descriptionHtml:
The Internal Product Analytics (IPA) team is the analytics backbone of Datadog's Product organization. With over thirty products on a single platform, IPA gives PMs and leadership the data, tooling, platform, and analysis they need to make good decisions. The team owns the recurring analytical work the Product org runs on and builds the AI-first workflows that make that analysis faster and more consistent across the org.

As Manager of the Internal Product Analytics team, you will directly manage a team of data analysts, partner closely with the PMs your team serves, and partner with the associated platform engineering teams. You will set the direction for how the team delivers analysis, builds AI-first tooling, and partners across functions. This is a role for someone who works well across teams, turning complex data and open questions into clear, trusted answers that PMs and leadership can act on.

What You'll Do:

  • Guide and grow the Internal Product Analytics team. Manage, coach, and develop a team of data analysts. Set priorities, hold a high bar for quality, and make sure the team's output is trusted across the Product org.

  • Partner directly with the PM org. Work side by side with the PMs your team serves to frame the questions that matter, shape the analysis, and make sure the answers reach them in a form they can act on.

  • Own the recurring analytics the PM org runs on. Business reviews, feature request analysis, usage and adoption tracking, and pricing analysis. Make this work consistent, repeatable, and fast so PMs get answers when they need them.

  • Build AI-first analytics. Design and ship AI-powered workflows and agents that do the heavy lifting of analysis, from data querying to synthesis to reporting. Set the standard for how the team uses AI so analysis scales without simply adding headcount.

  • Partner across functions. Work with Finance, Data Platform, Engineering, and Revenue teams to align on definitions, source the right data, and turn raw signals into decisions. Build trust with partners who do not report to you.

  • Turn data into decisions for leadership. Query product, CRM, and financial data to surface the insights that matter, then present them clearly to PMs and senior leadership so they can act with confidence.

  • Set the standard for product analytics across the org. Define the metrics, definitions, and analytical frameworks that leadership and every PM rely on, and own them as the single source of truth the Product org trusts.

Who You Are:

  • 6+ years in product analytics, data analytics, or a related field, with 2+ years managing or leading a team.

  • A strong track record partnering across functions (Product, Finance, Engineering, Data) and aligning stakeholders with different priorities toward shared outcomes.

  • Proven ability to partner directly with product managers as their analytics partner, turning product questions into analysis that informs decisions.

  • Fluent in SQL and comfortable in a modern data warehouse and BI tooling. You can go from raw data to a defensible answer yourself, not just direct others to do it.

  • Hands-on experience building or deploying AI-first analytics: AI-powered workflows, agents, or tooling that speed up real analytical work. Professional use of AI tools such as Claude, including prompt design and putting AI into day-to-day analysis.

  • Experience communicating with and presenting to senior leadership at the VP+ level, both in writing and in live settings.

  • Comfortable in ambiguous environments where you define the approach, prove value quickly, and iterate, rather than maintain an existing playbook.

  • Able to lead through influence rather than authority, building trust and driving outcomes across teams you do not directly manage.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting a product management org or working inside a Product function.

  • Familiarity with the modern data stack (for example dbt, Snowflake, semantic layers) and with product data and CRM systems.

  • Experience building or deploying AI agents or automated analytical workflows using current frameworks.

  • A background in analytics engineering or data platform work.

  • Experience with financial and revenue data (ARR, cohort analysis) and partnering closely with Finance.

  • Familiarity with Datadog's products and services.

title: IT Support Technician Intern
descriptionHtml:
The Enterprise IT Support team is responsible for the hardware and software that Datadog employees around the world use on a daily basis to successfully do their jobs.

As an Enterprise IT Support intern, you will combine theoretical learning at your school with practical, hands-on experience in our IT Support team. Over the course of your internship, you will progressively take on more responsibilities while helping ensure our ever-growing user base has everything they need to do their job. You’ll also gain exposure to security-adjacent tasks relevant to IT support operations.

  • Learn and assist in providing customer service and technical support for our employees
  • Shadow and support laptop deployment as part of onboarding and refresh cycles
  • Shadow and support laptop collection and account deactivation as part of employee offboarding cycles
  • Participate in new hire orientations to understand policies, best practices and services used within Datadog
  • Assist with general ticketing, account management, and basic troubleshooting under supervision
  • Help maintain hardware and software inventory
  • Contribute to documentation creation and maintenance
  • Observe and support unified communications setups in conference rooms and common areas
  • Participate in team meetings and knowledge-sharing sessions
  • Gain exposure to deployment and security-related projects
    • Support multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA) setup and troubleshooting for employees
    • Observe and support endpoint device enrollment using mobile device management (MDM) tools
    • Gain familiarity with access management principles, including the processes used to grant, review, and revoke employee access
    • Assist in following established procedures when responding to basic IT Security incidents under supervision
    • Participate in identity verification processes
  • Develop skills in various SaaS tools and IT workflows

Who You Are:

  • You will graduate in 2027 with a degree in IT, Cybersecurity field

descriptionHtml:

title: Commercial & Mid-Market Sales Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Datadog Sales Engineer 는 고객 및 파트너와의 기회를 검증하고 성사시키는 데 도움을 줍니다. 영업 프레젠테이션, 제품 데모, 기술 평가(POC) 지원을 통해 기술 전문 지식을 제공합니다. Sale Engineer 는 제품 팀과 함께 고객, 경쟁사, 파트너의 의견을 바탕으로 기능의 우선순위를 정하는 데 도움을 줍니다. 또한 다양한 팀과 협력하여 고객의 문제를 해결하고, 버그 문제를 에스컬레이션하며, 브랜드 홍보대사로서의 역할도 수행하게 됩니다. 무한한 잠재력을 지닌 친절하고 열정적인 팀에 합류하고 싶은 분들의 많은 지원 바랍니다!

Datadog은 사무실 문화를 통해 구축되는 관계와 협업, 창의성을 중시합니다. 우리는 데이터독 직원들이 자신에게 가장 적합한 일과 삶의 조화를 이룰 수 있도록 하이브리드 업무 환경을 운영하고 있습니다.

담당 업무

  • 영업팀과 협력하여 고객에게 전반적인 Datadog 가치 제안, 비전 및 전략을 명확하게 전달 
  • 경쟁력 있는 지식, 기술력 및 신뢰를 구축하기 위해 지속적으로 새로운 기술을 학습 
  • 잠재 고객을 대상으로 제품 및 기술 프레젠테이션 제공
  • 제품 팀과 직접 소통하여 기능 요청에 대해 협업 
  • 고객의 제품 온보딩을 돕고 장애물이 있을 때 지원 
  • 사전 판매 수명 주기 동안 다양한 기술적 과제에 대해 창의적으로 생각 

자격 요건

  • DevOps 모니터링 또는 아키텍처 도구에 대한 지식과 경험이 풍부한 분 
  • 외부 고객 또는 내부 팀에게 기술 프레젠테이션/데모를 편안하고 자신감 있게 전달 가능한 분
  • 다양한 문제를 창의적으로 해결하고, 매일 새로운 것을 배우는 것을 즐기는 분
  • Windows 또는 Linux  시스템 관리 경험 
  • DevSecOps 체계를 직접 구축하고 운영해본 경험 우대
  • 모의 해킹이나 신규 취약점 발견 시 개발팀에 설명하고 함께 대응 방안을 도출해본 경험 우대 
  • 고객을 직접 만나기 위한 출장 업무에 익숙한 분

Datadog은 모든 계층의 사람들을 소중히 여깁니다. 모든 사람이 입사 첫날에 위의 모든 자격 요건을 충족하지 못할 수도 있습니다. 괜찮습니다. 기술에 대한 열정이 있고 자신의 역량을 키우고 싶다면 지원하실 것을 권장합니다.

혜택 및 성장: 

  • 최우수한 수준의 온보딩
  • 풍성한 글로벌 혜택
  • 사내 네트워킹을 위한 부서 내 멘토 및 버디 프로그램
  • 신규 채용 우리사주(RSU) 및 직원 주식 매입 계획(ESPP)

descriptionHtml:
As a Director, Enterprise Sales Engineering, you will lead a team of frontline leaders, driving account strategy, deal execution, operational excellence, and team development across your region. 

This is a strategic leadership role with regional impact within North America. You will act as a force multiplier by owning team and region performance, shaping execution standards, and partnering closely with Sales leadership to influence go to market strategy, improve outcomes, and scale impact beyond individual deals. 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own in-field execution at a regional level by taking an executive presence role in strategic and high-impact opportunities and providing senior-level stakeholder alignment and technical credibility alongside your team. 
  • Develop and operationalize a repeatable formula and methodology that can scale across a large customer base, enabling Datadog to accelerate enterprise growth by illustrating to customers how Datadog’s observability and security solutions quickly, simply, and efficiently deliver measurable business outcomes especially in a world increasingly dominated by Agentic AI.
  • Partner confidently with senior Sales leadership on regional strategy, multi-quarter planning, annual capacity planning, and forecast alignment operating 2-3 quarters ahead to anticipate resourcing needs and business priorities.
  • Oversee consistent, high-quality delivery across technical sales cycles in the region, including evaluations, customer engagements, and deal progression.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Sales Engineering leaders, driving performance, engagement, and long-term career growth through regular feedback and structured development.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Marketing, Enablement, and Support at a senior level to align on regional strategy, GTM execution, and customer experience.

  • Track competitive developments, market dynamics, and emerging technologies to ensure the team is equipped to position Datadog as a leader in cloud security.

  • 5+ years of experience leading frontline SE leaders in a customer-facing technical organization with proven ability to manage team performance, develop team members, and scale high-performing teams.

title: Technical Escalations Engineer II (RUM) - APJ
descriptionHtml:
As Datadog’s in-house product experts, the Technical Escalation Engineering (TEE) team plays a critical role in driving our global success. We enable our customers, from the world’s most innovative startups to the largest enterprises.

Through deep technical expertise, relentless problem-solving, and exceptional customer engagement, we educate, guide, and troubleshoot, delivering high-impact solutions that shape the customer experience. Whether through hands-on technical call, in-depth fact findings meeting, or complex investigations, we set the gold standard for technical excellence and customer advocacy.

As part of our TEE team, you’ll tackle the most challenging technical problems, collaborate directly with Engineering and Product to refine and evolve our platform, and mentor teams worldwide, elevating the technical bar at every level.

As part of the Technical Escalation Engineering (TEE) team, you’ll operate at the heart of Datadog’s ecosystem, working at the intersection of Technical Solutions, Engineering, Product, and our Customers. Every challenge you take on will directly impact the performance, scalability, and success of both our clients and our platform. You’ll be in an environment that moves fast, challenges you daily, and rewards curiosity, ownership, and technical excellence.

This is your chance to shape the future of observability and security, driving innovation, mentoring teams, and influencing product direction while witnessing your expertise make an immediate and lasting impact.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. 

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop deep technical expertise and continuously learn as the product evolves.
  • Investigate complex escalations, lead high-stakes technical calls, and drive solutions for our most critical customer challenges with urgency and precision.
  • Run engaging office hours, deliver impactful learning sessions, and mentor the Global Support Engineering team (GSE), ensuring they’re equipped to handle any challenge.
  • Partner with Engineering and Product to proactively identify gaps, drive improvements, and advocate for customers in shaping the evolution of our platform.
  • Become a trusted resource on Real User Monitoring, handling escalations, guiding troubleshooting, and driving resolutions.
  • Lead investigations into session-related issues, telemetry gaps, SDK behavior inconsistencies, or performance metrics anomalies.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to escalate issues, validate improvements, and influence the roadmap based on real-world use cases.
  • Contribute to internal tooling, playbooks, and enablement resources that scale RUM knowledge across the Solutions team.
  • Grow your expertise in platform-specific behavior (e.g., JS frameworks, native mobile SDKs) while keeping a strong focus on holistic end-user experience.

 Who You Are:

  • A self-driven problem solver with an obsession for excellence and continuous learning. You thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and push beyond expectations.
  • A strategic thinker who defaults to a client-centric approach, proactively identifying opportunities to enhance customer experience while balancing technical feasibility.
  • An independent, fast learner, capable of picking up new technologies, adapting to evolving priorities, and crafting innovative solutions to complex technical issues.
  • A collaborator and mentor, who enjoys sharing knowledge, raising the technical bar for the team, and contributing to a culture of excellence.
  • Passionate about end-user experience and observability, with a solid understanding of how performance, behavior, and telemetry connect across web and mobile platforms.
  • Familiar with client-side instrumentation and telemetry collection, whether it’s through browser-based SDKs or mobile app integrations.
  • Comfortable investigating issues like missing sessions, incorrect tagging, data sampling, or signal noise across different runtime environments.
  • Analytical and resourceful, capable of reproducing customer environments and digging into logs, SDK behavior, and performance patterns.
  • Eager to grow deeper expertise in either web or mobile RUM, with a strong foundation and the mindset to learn both.
  • Computer Science or Engineering majors
  • Experienced in using Zendesk, Jira, Confluence, or similar softwares.
  • Familiarity with Datadog, integrations ecosystem, or similar observability platforms is a strong plus.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager
descriptionHtml:
TPMs at Datadog see the problems hiding between teams, engineer away the work that shouldn’t require humans, and drive the company’s most technically complex and consequential bets to completion.


Technical Program Management at Datadog operates at the intersection of engineering depth and organizational reach by driving high priority, cross-functional programs that are too complex and consequential for any single team to own. We partner with engineering on solving deeply technical problems at scale by connecting the people, decisions, and context to move Datadog's most important work forward.


We build the systems and automation that make entire classes of program work self-executing. We are in the architecture conversation early, earning trust through technical judgment. We use AI to surface risks earlier, accelerate program execution plans, and find cross-team patterns that would otherwise stay hidden. The faster teams move, the more essential it is to have someone who can operate across them.


At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.


What We Expect:

These are the expectations we hold for every TPM at Datadog.

  • Technical depth, product domain expertise, and AI systems literacy; knowing how AI solutions work, where they fail, and the scope and impact of those failures. AI brings more complexity into the picture - the technical bar is higher, not lower.

  • Build the systems that reduce the need for coordination

  • Identify what matters before anyone asks, and automate the rest

  • Engineer program lifecycles end-to-end

  • See what no single team can see and own the solution

  • Drive the company's most technically complex and consequential bets through cross-functional agreement, organizational visibility, and influence

  • Build AI powered automation tools and deploy them at every stage of program execution


What You'll Do:

See Across: Identify What No Single Team Can See

  • Own large cross-functional programs spanning multiple engineering orgs, product, and business functions

  • Proactively surface systemic risks, cross-pod dependencies, and organizational friction before they become escalations

  • Build and maintain SVP-level visibility through tracked KPIs on Datadog’s highest-priority initiatives

  • Uses technical credibility, trusted relationships, and product domain expertise to bridge the gaps between functions where misalignment is expensive

Engineer Away: Automate What Shouldn’t Require Humans

  • Identify repeatable program archetypes and engineer the lifecycle end-to-end with AI solutions; the goal is to make the program run itself

  • Build automation that reduces the need for coordination, eliminating program overhead so engineers and PMs spend time only on work requiring human judgment

  • Contribute to the TPM toolkit: AI-powered risk synthesis, dependency tracking, stakeholder mapping, and program templates

  • Drive the shift from manual coordination to self-executing program infrastructure

Drive Completion: Move The Company’s Most Complex Bets Forward

  • Lead programs across four archetypes: deep technical, large cross-functional, product delivery, and operational

  • Accelerate alignment by removing friction and overhead, not by adding process.

  • Hold the judgment call on when to escalate, when to slow down, when a technical decision has organizational implications

  • Own outcomes, not activities - your value is measured by what ships and what never had the chance to become a problem


Who You Are:

Required

  • 5+ years of technical program management at a high-growth technology company

  • Demonstrated ability to drive large, ambiguous, cross-functional programs to completion with minimal direction

  • Engineering credibility earned through hands-on experience with technically complex domains — observability, infrastructure, data platforms, or AI/ML systems including model training pipelines, ML infrastructure, and GPU compute. You can go deep on architecture and system design, push back on technical decisions, and hold your own in the room with staff engineers and senior ICs.

  • Track record of earning trust with senior engineering and product leadership - not through title, through judgment

  • Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable owning the narrative at VP+ levels

  • Active AI practitioner, you use AI tools in your daily work and can demonstrate how they’ve changed your leverage

  • You have built something, a tool, a template, an automated workflow, that other people use

Strong Signal

  • You identified a systemic problem no one asked you to find and built the operating system to solve it

  • You automated a program lifecycle or workflow that previously required manual coordination

  • You have operated in observability, infrastructure, data platforms, or AI/ML environments and can speak to the technical architecture, not just the program execution

  • You have managed programs with real unit economics implications - cloud cost, capacity, margin

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.


Benefits and Growth:

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

  • Assigned TPM mentor and engineering buddy program for learning and relationship building

  • An inclusive company culture, active Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups), in-person team summits, local office programming

  • Competitive global benefits; free, mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

title: Senior Accounts Receivable Analyst
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Accounts Receivable Analyst to join our Revenue Team. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in accounts receivable, exceptional analytical abilities, and a keen attention to detail. This role will be responsible for managing a book of business and addressing internal and external concerns via email and Zendesk. Partnering with internal stakeholders such as Customer Success, Revenue and Sales, you will assist in resolving Billing disputes.

Senior Accounts Receivable Analysts have the opportunity to grow their careers in Finance and continue contributing to Datadog team success.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage the accounts receivable collections process for assigned book of business
  • Analyze customer payment patterns and aging reports to identify trends and potential issues
  • Collaborate with internal teams to resolve billing discrepancies and disputes in a timely manner
  • Manage incoming billing inquiries and collectability concerns through Zendesk. Triage accordingly to Revenue, Sales, and Customer Success teams and to drive collections
  • Develop and maintain effective relationships with clients to facilitate prompt payment and resolve outstanding balances
  • Help customers understand their bills, which vary with usage and plan type
  • Assist with external audit, compliance and special projects as necessary
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior members of the accounts receivable team.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting or equivalent required
  • 5+ years of full cycle Accounts Receivable  / Billing Operations experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel required
  • Ability to work independently, with a strong work ethic, self-motivation and problem-solving skills
  • Attention to detail and high level of accuracy
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal; position is highly visible in the company

title: Senior Sales Engineer - FED
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Federal Enterprise Sales Engineer, you'll be a trusted technical advisor to federal customers and Sales. You'll help agencies connect mission priorities, modernization programs, and operational risks to technical solutions. You'll lead complex evaluations in regulated environments and shape the technical strategy for opportunities across hybrid, on-premises, and public cloud environments.

You'll own the technical evaluation experience from discovery through decision. You'll influence agency stakeholders and coordinate with systems integrators, resellers, and technology partners. You'll help customers and account teams address security, compliance, acquisition, and deployment requirements while setting accurate expectations about capabilities, prerequisites, and solution design.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the sales process in partnership with Account Executives by leading and shaping the technical strategy across opportunities from PG to Closed Won
  • Lead discovery throughout the sales cycle to uncover technical challenges, mission and business goals, decision criteria, and success measures, then shape solution strategy and measurable business outcomes within applicable security, compliance, acquisition, and deployment requirements
  • Deliver engaging product demos, technical presentations, and solution workshops that connect platform capabilities to customer outcomes for diverse stakeholder audiences including executives
  • Own the technical strategy and response quality for RFIs, RFPs, proposal responses, and architecture reviews. Coordinate internal teams and partners to keep claims, dependencies, and deployment assumptions accurate and appropriately scoped
  • Full ownership of the technical evaluations (POVs) end-to-end: scoping use cases and requirements, defining competitive success criteria, aligning agency and partner stakeholders, building a project plan with clear timelines and decision points, surfacing risks and dependencies, and holding all participants accountable to the process
  • Identify, develop, and leverage technical champions across multi-stakeholder environments, building a structured plan for champion cultivation and influence throughout the deal cycle 
  • Contribute to product direction through active participation in structured product and engineering field feedback sessions, bringing field insights and customer patterns to PM and engineering teams
  • Drive operational excellence by ensuring activity, deal progress, and customer interactions are accurately documented and up to date in related systems 
  • Identify and proactively resolve technical and organizational blockers by collaborating across Product, Support, and GTM teams before customers are impacted
  • Contribute to team enablement by mentoring peers, sharing best practices, and creating reusable assets that scale knowledge across the region

Who You Are: 

  • 7+ years of experience in Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or a technical customer-facing role within an enterprise environment
  • Experience leading complex federal sales cycles and technical evaluations involving agency stakeholders, systems integrators, resellers, and technology partners
  • Skilled at influencing and adapting communication across technical, business, and executive audiences 
  • Advanced background in hybrid environments and public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), Kubernetes, APM/tracing, security, developer experience, and observability
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • A consultative, outcome-oriented approach to problem-solving and customer engagement
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple opportunities and priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience mentoring peers or contributing to team enablement initiatives
  • Demonstrated capability of utilizing AI tooling and scaling it 
  • Growth mindset of embracing change and being curious 
  • Willingness to travel as needed to support customer engagements

title: Senior Enablement Program Manager, Sales Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The Technical Solutions (TS) Enablement team empowers Datadog's global post-sales organization—including Support, Customer Success, and Sales Engineering—with the skills, tools, and resources they need to deliver world-class customer outcomes. As a Senior TS Enablement Program Manager supporting Sales Engineering, you'll own the design and execution of complex, high-visibility enablement programs that drive lasting change across the TS organization. You'll operate with significant autonomy, lead cross-functional initiatives, and serve as a senior voice within the Enablement team—partnering closely with leadership to translate business priorities into measurable enablement impact at scale.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end strategy and execution for complex, global enablement programs—managing multiple concurrent workstreams across regions, functions, and timelines with limited guidance.
  • Lead cross-functional stakeholder relationships with senior partners across StratOps, Product, TS Leadership, and the People Team—negotiating scope, aligning on priorities, and driving accountability without positional authority.
  • Translate business goals and OKRs into multi-quarter program roadmaps; communicate priorities, trade-offs, and progress to leadership with clarity and a clear point of view.
  • Design and implement comprehensive metrics frameworks to measure change adoption and program effectiveness; pull and analyze Salesforce and LMS data to track performance against KPIs; present findings to senior stakeholders and iterate for lasting impact.
  • Build and deliver executive-ready materials that tell a compelling business story—translating complex data, program updates, and regional insights into structured narratives with clear recommendations.
  • Conduct ongoing needs assessments, stakeholder interviews, and pulse checks across TS regions; synthesize qualitative and quantitative feedback to inform program strategy and surface emerging gaps.
  • Design the tools, resources, communications, and training frameworks needed to support TS workflow changes at scale—partnering with Curriculum and Field teams on content development and delivery.
  • Partner with Sales Engineering leadership to design ramp and enablement programs that account for differences in deal complexity and skill development across the Sales Engineering org.
  • Mentor and develop junior EPM ICs on the team—providing structured feedback on program design and stakeholder management, and raising the quality bar across program work.
  • Identify and implement AI-powered workflows, automations, and process improvements that increase the efficiency, consistency, and scalability of enablement programs—from reporting and data pipelines to content creation and stakeholder communications.
  • Maintain a deep, current understanding of regional needs, TS team performance, and functional priorities to ensure programs remain relevant and impactful across a global audience.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6–8 years of related experience in enablement, program management, change management, or a closely related field—or a Master’s degree with 4+ years.
  • Proven track record leading complex, multi-quarter programs with high visibility—comfortable operating independently and making sound judgment calls with limited oversight.

title: Curriculum Manager
descriptionHtml:
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Enablement Curriculum and working across a cross-functional Enablement team, you'll build learning experiences that hold up in the field - objectives, practice, assessment, and the content that carries them. This is a builder's role. You'll decide how the learning actually works, and you'll own the quality of what ships.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

Who you are:

  • An owner: You take pride in your outputs and their outcomes. You take ownership from design through launch and everything that comes after it.
  • An innovator: You challenge the status quo, bring new ideas, and look for ways to improve what already exists.
  • An agile problem solver: You shift seamlessly between detail and big picture to meet the moment, adapting to change with a solutions-oriented mindset.
  • A lifelong learner: You challenge assumptions and use curiosity to drive continuous improvement.
  • A trusted advisor: You ask sharp questions, synthesize complex ideas, and build relationships to understand and explain ambiguous concepts.
  • A clear communicator: You bring structure, clarity and polish to your work - written, verbal or visual.

What you’ll do:

  • Build the curriculum for Global Commercial Customer Success. Develop high-quality enablement content (instructor-led materials, facilitator guides, eLearning, job aids and assessments) for both individual contributors and their frontline leaders, built to instructional design and adult learning principles.
  • Build within the learner journey. Contribute to and build the components of role-specific journeys (onboarding, everboarding and on-demand) inside the curriculum arc for your area.
  • Know what good looks like. Translate performance expectations into observable behaviors and clear proficiency standards.
  • Turn business problems into learning design. Partner with Program Management and Strategy & Operations to identify the key behaviors and knowledge a program needs to shift, and design the learning that gets there.
  • Own the learning objectives for the programs you build, and design assessments that measure against them.
  • Build programs that drive durable behavior change. Design practice, reinforcement and refresher paths into programs.
  • Develop content with build partners and other Enablement teams, including subject matter experts who don't report to you, and manage your build schedule so programs meet quality standards and timelines.
  • Partner with facilitators, operations teams and test audiences to ensure successful rollouts of new and updated programs.
  • Help maintain the programs you build, keeping content accurate, current and consistent after launch.
  • Use AI well. Use AI for scripting, storyboards, assessment drafting and learner-feedback analysis, and coach peers on responsible AI-assisted content creation.

Your experience:

  • 3–5 years in Enablement, Learning & Development, Sales/Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Instructional Design or similar (bonus points for a combination)
  • Proven track record designing and building enablement content with measurable learner impact
  • Working knowledge of adult learning principles and a learning design methodology (e.g. ADDIE or equivalent)
  • Ability to design clean, intuitive learning materials across modalities — instructor-led, eLearning, simulation, job aids — blending instructional and visual design
  • Ability to manage multi-week content projects independently and deliver quality on short timeframes
  • Experience partnering with subject matter experts and stakeholders in a go-to-market organization
  • Comfort using learner data — completion, assessment and feedback — to find gaps and improve programs
  • Understanding of sales processes and challenges in a high-velocity environment
  • Familiarity with at least one sales methodology (e.g. Command of the Message, MEDDICC, Sandler, Challenger, value-based selling) or equivalent

Bonus Points:

  • Experience in Sales, Sales Development, Sales Leadership or Sales Operations
  • Formal grounding in instructional design and adult learning (e.g. ATD CPTD, CPLP or equivalent)
  • Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS or technology company
  • Experience with an LMS and content authoring tools
  • Experience building content that other people facilitate
  • Basic understanding of the observability, DevOps or cloud space

descriptionHtml:

Our Security Partner Manager will identify, onboard and establish joint sales and GTM acceleration with the regions to Security-focussed SIs, VARs, MSSP and Consultancies, supported by a brand new Partner Program, partner investments, and a strong team of Partner Solution Architects, Marketers, and Success Managers. title: Curriculum Manager (EMEA)
descriptionHtml:
Datadog is looking for a Curriculum Manager to build and manage enablement curriculum for our EMEA Sales and Customer Success teams.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Sales Enablement Curriculum and working across a cross-functional Enablement team, you'll build learning experiences that hold up in the field - objectives, practice, assessment, and the content that carries them. This is a builder's role. You'll decide how the learning actually works, and you'll own the quality of what ships.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

Who you are:

  • An owner: You take pride in your outputs and their outcomes. You take ownership from design through launch and everything that comes after it.
  • An innovator: You challenge the status quo, bring new ideas, and look for ways to improve what already exists.
  • An agile problem solver: You shift seamlessly between detail and big picture to meet the moment, adapting to change with a solutions-oriented mindset.
  • A lifelong learner: You challenge assumptions and use curiosity to drive continuous improvement.
  • A trusted advisor: You ask sharp questions, synthesize complex ideas, and build relationships to understand and explain ambiguous concepts.
  • A clear communicator: You bring structure, clarity and polish to your work - written, verbal or visual.

What you’ll do:

  • Build the curriculum for EMEA Commercial Sales and Customer Success. Develop high-quality enablement content (instructor-led materials, facilitator guides, eLearning, job aids and assessments) for both individual contributors and their frontline leaders, built to instructional design and adult learning principles.
  • Build within the learner journey. Contribute to and build the components of role-specific journeys (onboarding, everboarding and on-demand) inside the curriculum arc for your area.
  • Know what good looks like. Translate performance expectations into observable behaviors and clear proficiency standards.
  • Turn business problems into learning design. Partner with Program Management and Strategy & Operations to identify the key behaviors and knowledge a program needs to shift, and design the learning that gets there.
  • Own the learning objectives for the programs you build, and design assessments that measure against them.
  • Build programs that drive durable behavior change. Design practice, reinforcement and refresher paths into programs.
  • Develop content with build partners and other Enablement teams, including subject matter experts who don't report to you, and manage your build schedule so programs meet quality standards and timelines.
  • Partner with facilitators, operations teams and test audiences to ensure successful rollouts of new and updated programs.
  • Help maintain the programs you build, keeping content accurate, current and consistent after launch.
  • Use AI well. Use AI for scripting, storyboards, assessment drafting and learner-feedback analysis, and coach peers on responsible AI-assisted content creation.

Your experience:

  • 4–5 years in Enablement, Learning & Development, Sales, Revenue Operations or similar (bonus points for a combination)
  • Proven track record designing and building enablement content with measurable learner impact
  • Working knowledge of adult learning principles and a learning design methodology (e.g. ADDIE or equivalent)
  • Ability to design clean, intuitive learning materials across modalities — instructor-led, eLearning, simulation, job aids — blending instructional and visual design
  • Ability to manage multi-week content projects independently and deliver quality on short timeframes
  • Experience partnering with subject matter experts and stakeholders in a go-to-market organization
  • Comfort using learner data — completion, assessment and feedback — to find gaps and improve programs
  • Understanding of sales processes and challenges in a high-velocity environment
  • Familiarity with at least one sales methodology (e.g. Command of the Message, MEDDICC, Sandler, Challenger, value-based selling) or equivalent

Bonus Points:

  • Experience in Sales, Sales Development, Sales Leadership or Sales Operations
  • Formal grounding in instructional design and adult learning (e.g. ATD CPTD, CPLP or equivalent)
  • Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS or technology company
  • Experience with an LMS and content authoring tools
  • Experience building content that other people facilitate
  • Basic understanding of the observability, DevOps or cloud space

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan

title: Senior Field Enablement Manager
descriptionHtml:
The Team

Our GTM Enablement team plays a critical role in helping Datadog's Sales and Customer Success teams succeed by equipping them with the right skills, knowledge, and tools at the right time. We partner closely with teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Curriculum, and Operations to ensure enablement programs translate into real performance in the field.

If you like adding value and seeing the direct impact of your work, and you thrive in dynamic environments where you can roll up your sleeves and get things done, this role is for you.

The Opportunity

Datadog's Enterprise business across EMEA continues to scale, and we're looking for a Field Enablement Manager to deliver ongoing ramp and everboarding enablement for Enterprise sellers across key EMEA markets (including the UK, DACH, France, Benelux, and the Nordics) — ensuring global enablement programs land effectively amid complex, multi-country Enterprise deals.

You'll serve as a trusted partner to Enterprise Sales leaders, adapting global programs to the realities of the EMEA Enterprise motion — longer sales cycles, multi-stakeholder buying committees, and a diverse regional footprint — while staying tightly aligned with our global Field Enablement organization.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives operating independently, builds strong relationships in the field, and enjoys adapting enablement programs to meet the needs of a fast-growing, sophisticated Enterprise segment.

What You'll Do

  • Deliver live and virtual enablement sessions and implement training programs focused on ongoing ramp and everboarding that improve the performance and productivity of Enterprise sellers and leaders across EMEA.
  • Administer program certifications — score and evaluate submissions against established rubrics and provide structured feedback.
  • Conduct ongoing field listening (shadows, 1:1s, syncs with first-line leaders) to maintain a strong pulse on Enterprise business needs, gaps, and strengths across EMEA markets; share insights with the broader enablement team to shape programs and priorities.
  • Lead reinforcement and coaching to drive post-program adoption, including designing activities (role plays, deal clinics, skill practice sessions) that connect training to measurable behavior change in real, complex customer scenarios.
  • Partner with Curriculum, Program Management, and Operations to share field insights and pilot or co-build content, and work closely with first-line Enterprise Sales leaders to build trusted relationships, diagnose challenges, and deliver ad hoc training in response to emerging needs.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate delivery and reinforcement — including synthesizing field feedback and surfacing patterns — and model effective AI use for the teams you train.

Who You Are

  • 4–5 years of experience in sales enablement, field enablement, training, or a related GTM role, with a proven delivery track record supporting Enterprise Sales and/or Customer Success teams in a SaaS or technology environment; multi-country EMEA experience is a strong plus.
  • Strong understanding of Datadog and/or the broader technology industry, including foundational knowledge of Datadog's core product pillars (Infrastructure, APM, Logs) and the ability to connect product capabilities to Enterprise customer value.
  • Strong facilitator with experience delivering engaging live and virtual training sessions to senior, sophisticated audiences, and familiarity with Enterprise sales methodologies/frameworks such as MEDDICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, Sandler, etc. (certification a plus).
  • Solid business acumen and comfort using performance data, field feedback, and qualitative insights to inform enablement decisions; experience with Asana or similar project management tools is a plus.
  • Highly collaborative and relationship-oriented — you build trust quickly with sellers, managers, and cross-functional partners.
  • Organized, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently across a large, diverse region.
  • Fluent in English, with proficiency in one or more additional European languages a plus; willing and able to travel approximately 25% across EMEA.

Why This Role Matters

As a Field Enablement Manager supporting Datadog's EMEA Enterprise business, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring our global enablement programs translate into local impact for some of our most strategic sellers and customers. You'll help accelerate ramp, build seller confidence, and enable Enterprise teams to succeed with customers across one of Datadog's fastest-growing and most complex regions.

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Applied Scientist - AI Platform
descriptionHtml:
AI Platform builds the foundations of Datadog's AI efforts. The org is 70+ people organised in three pillars: training and serving (GPU clusters, distributed training, low-level infrastructure), agents (agent harnesses, memory systems, the internal AI gateway that routes every LLM request at Datadog), and evaluation and experimentation. This role sits in the evaluation and experimentation pillar, which owns Datadog's shared annotation and evaluation infrastructure — including the evaluation scenario store and the telemetry archival systems used across the Bits org. Together they let an agent travel back in time and query what Datadog looked like at the exact moment an incident happened, so scenarios can be replayed and agent performance tracked over time.

Specifically, you'll be the first applied scientist on GenSim (Generative Simulations), the team that builds the environments Datadog's agents learn in. GenSim doesn't replay sampled telemetry — it stands up real, fully instrumented applications that talk to Datadog, drives them with representative traffic, injects controlled failures, and records what happens. Because GenSim injected the failure, it knows the ground truth. That corpus — hundreds of postmortem-derived scenarios and thousands of runnable applications — is today the primary source of post-training data for Datadog's own SRE model, and the substrate that Bits AI SRE and our other agents are trained and evaluated against.

The team has no applied science support today and is learning post-training data methodology on the fly. That's the gap this role fills, and the open questions are the interesting part. How do you tell whether a generated environment is actually representative of the messy, incomplete telemetry real customers run — rather than a suspiciously clean one where every monitor exists and every service emits complete logs? How do you make injected problems genuinely hard, and how do you even measure difficulty? How do you define and control the quality of post-training data when correctness, representativeness and difficulty pull in different directions? How do you evaluate an agent end to end when the trajectory is non-deterministic? Creating simulated agent environments for monitoring and SRE work is not well solved in open source or in published research, and Datadog is the leading company in this field. If those are the problems you want to spend your time on, come build this with us.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the applied science direction for GenSim: set the methodology and the forward-looking technical calls on how simulated environments and post-training data should be built, on a team where that decision-making does not exist yet.
  • Define, measure and raise the quality of post-training data — basic correctness, representativeness against the real distribution of customer systems and production telemetry, and difficulty — and make those measures something the team can act on release over release.
  • Close the realism gap. Simulated environments today are too clean and the injected problems are not yet hard enough; you'll drive the research and the engineering that make them look like real, imperfect production systems.
  • Build scalable, production-grade systems rather than research scripts. The output is not just a dataset — it is a system of synthetic environments that must be reliable and invokable inside a training loop.
  • Determine how this data is best applied, in LLM post-training and in evaluation, and own the agent and LLM application evaluation approaches for these environments.
  • Work cross-functionally with the engineers and applied scientists on adjacent teams — Bits AI SRE, the model training effort, and the wider evaluation and experimentation pillar — so that what you learn moves freely in both directions.

Who You Are:

  • You have a PhD, MS or equivalent research experience in a scientific field, with strong applied mathematics grounding.
  • 6+ years of relevant applied science or ML engineering experience, including setting technical direction for others.
  • You have hands-on experience with LLM and agent post-training data: how it is created, managed, and how training-data quality is controlled. This is the requirement that matters most.
  • You have real domain expertise in LLMs and agentic applications — not classical ML fine-tuning. Fine-tuning classifiers or traditional models is a different problem from the one this team is solving.
  • You have evaluated agents or LLM applications, and can define what 'good' means before you measure it.
  • You are a strong programmer and production software engineer. Python at minimum, plus the ability to ship scalable production systems and work with distributed systems.
  • You collaborate well across engineering and science teams, and you're comfortable being the domain expert who decides what comes next.
  • You thrive in ambiguity and can make sound technical calls when the path isn't yet defined.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on LLM fine-tuning, post-training or model training experience.
  • Background in statistics, experiment design and data analysis.
  • Experience deploying production-level ML infrastructure.
  • Observability or monitoring systems background.
  • Architecture-level understanding of LLMs.

title: Manager I, Engineering - Cloud FinOps
descriptionHtml:
Datadog's Cloud FinOps team answers a question the business runs on: what does each product and each customer actually cost us to serve? Finance uses this team's output to close Datadog's books, Product uses it to compare cost to serve against what a customer pays, and engineering leaders use it to catch cost movements before they compound. As the Engineering Manager for this team, you'll own delivery across the runtime pipeline, coverage onboarding, and cost-to-customer identity mapping. You'll own the contracts that Finance and platform teams depend on. The core engineering problem is reproducibility: every dollar of cloud cost is placed against the product and customer that caused it, with lineage on every result and closed periods that replay exactly. This role starts by closing a coverage gap and grows into owning the model every platform team at Datadog onboards through.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead and grow a team of engineers building the platform that allocates Datadog's cloud cost to products and customers, setting the operating rhythm across runtime and release, coverage onboarding, and identity and mapping.
  • Own the publication contract with Finance: versioned metrics with effective dates, backfill, and reproducible history, so any closed period can be replayed on demand and trusted for close.
  • Own the metric contracts with platform teams across Engineering, shifting cost facts to the teams that generate the cost so coverage growth stops scaling linearly with your headcount.
  • Partner with Revenue Engineering on the cost-to-revenue identity join that turns cost data into margin per product and per customer.
  • Drive continuous improvement in product and customer cost coverage and accuracy, and hold delivery commitments with teams that don't report to you.
  • Reduce key-person risk on runtime and compiler architecture by spreading ownership across the team, and use AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, and similar) to raise the team's speed and leverage.

Who You Are:

  • An engineering leader with experience managing data platform or data engineering teams building batch and pipeline systems judged on correctness and reproducibility.
  • You've shipped versioned publication with effective dates, backfill, and reproducible history.
  • You've held a delivery commitment with a team outside your reporting line, and you can describe what happened the first time a contract was missed.
  • You bring domain experience in metering, usage-based billing, cloud cost, revenue data, or financial data platforms.
  • You operate without a product manager in the loop on the external half of the job: you set the contracts, negotiate the boundaries, and drive the roadmap yourself.
  • If you've owned systems whose output is audited or closed by Finance (SOX scope, month-end close, revenue recognition), graph datasets or built retrieval-grounded systems where every answer cites its source and you know where a model shouldn't be trusted with a number at all, that is helpful experience.

title: Manager, Field Enablement EMEA
descriptionHtml:
The Team

Our GTM Enablement team plays a critical role in helping Datadog's Sales, SDR, and Customer Success teams succeed by equipping them with the right skills, knowledge, and tools at the right time. We partner closely with teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Curriculum, and Operations to ensure enablement programs translate into real performance in the field.

If you like adding value and seeing the direct impact of your work through the people you lead, and you thrive in dynamic environments where you can roll up your sleeves and get things done, this role is for you.

The Opportunity

Datadog is investing further in EMEA, and we're looking for a Manager, Field Enablement to lead our team of Field Enablement Managers supporting Sales, SDR, and Customer Success across the region — a frontline people leadership role where you'll manage, coach, and grow your team while helping execute the enablement strategy and quality bar for EMEA.

You'll partner closely with EMEA Sales, SDR, and Customer Success leadership, as well as Enablement Curriculum, Program Management, and Operations teams, to translate regional priorities into a coordinated enablement plan across markets and segments — keeping your team's programs tightly aligned with our global Field Enablement standards.

This role is ideal for someone who has excelled in field/sales enablement and leadership, cares as much about developing enablement practitioners as developing sellers and CSMs, and wants to help build the enablement leadership layer for one of Datadog's fastest-growing regions.

What You'll Do

  • Spearhead the Field Sales Enablement team’s transition from facilitators/trainers to data-driven business partners and coaches who are able to proactively identify GTM knowledge/performance gaps and deliver targeted enablement solutions that drive behavior change
  • Manage, coach, and develop your team of Field Enablement Managers — regular 1:1s, goal-setting, performance feedback, and career growth plans calibrated against the Field Enablement career path.
  • Own workforce planning for the EMEA team, including recruiting, interviewing, and onboarding new Field Enablement Managers as headcount and market coverage scale.
  • Set the enablement strategy and priorities for EMEA in partnership with Sales, SDR, and Customer Success leadership, translating regional business goals into a coordinated plan across your team.
  • Establish and maintain a consistent quality bar for delivery — facilitation standards, coaching rigor, program effectiveness, and AI fluency — through practice sessions, calibration exercises, and delivery reviews.
  • Serve as the strategic partner and escalation point for EMEA Sales, SDR, and CS leaders, coaching your team to turn field listening into insight that shapes enablement priorities and regional recommendations.
  • Keep EMEA aligned with the global Field Enablement organization: partner with the Director and other regional leaders on standards and certifications, represent EMEA in global forums, and report team impact and outcomes to stakeholders.

Who You Are

  • 7+ years of experience in sales enablement, field enablement, training, or a related GTM role, including direct experience as a Field Enablement Manager or equivalent senior individual contributor.
  • Prior experience managing people directly, or clear, demonstrated readiness to step into people management — including experience hiring, onboarding, and scaling a team, ideally in a fast-growing or newly-formed function.
  • Deep understanding of the EMEA GTM landscape, with experience supporting Sales, SDR, and/or Customer Success teams across multiple markets and languages.
  • Track record of partnering with senior Sales, SDR, and CS leadership to translate business priorities into enablement strategy, backed by excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influence skills.
  • Strong coaching orientation — certified coach (e.g., ICF ACC/PCC, Co-Active CTI, or equivalent) preferred, or a demonstrated commitment to developing one — paired with expert facilitation experience and familiarity with sales methodologies (MEDDICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, Sandler, etc.).
  • Data-driven approach to enablement — comfortable using sales performance data, field feedback, and qualitative insights to set priorities and measure impact; experience with Asana or similar project management tools is a plus.
  • Fluent in English (additional European languages a strong plus), and willing and able to travel approximately 30% across EMEA.

Why This Role Matters

As the first people leader for Datadog's EMEA Field Enablement team, you'll build the leadership layer that helps a growing team of Field Enablement Managers do their best work — and, in turn, help Sales, SDR, and Customer Success teams across EMEA ramp faster, sell better, and retain more customers. You'll shape how enablement scales as a function in one of Datadog's most complex and fastest-growing regions, with a direct line to the Director of Field Sales & CS Enablement.

title: Staff Product Manager - Self Improving Software
descriptionHtml:
As a Staff Product Manager on Datadog's Self-Improving Products team, you will take a new product family from zero to one: a closed loop that watches how a customer's software and its users behave, ranks what is worth changing, proposes the change, proves whether it worked, and carries the result into the next cycle. Datadog already holds every piece this product needs, including behavioral data from Product Analytics and Session Replay, full-stack telemetry from APM, Log Management, Error Tracking, and Continuous Profiler, rollout control through Feature Flags and Experimentation, and a coding agent in Bits AI Dev Agent that opens verified pull requests from production signal. You will own assembling these into one product where the loop closes on its own. This is founding work with no precedent inside Datadog, and an opportunity to grow as a product leader by shaping the scope, recruiting the first design partners, and setting the quality bar for an AI-native product from the ground up.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Set product direction for a new product family by defining the problems and desired outcomes, and partnering with engineering to find the narrowest first slice that proves the loop closes and delivers value to customers in phases.
  • Own the product decisions at every stage of the loop: what signal is trustworthy enough to trigger an automated change, which opportunities rank highest and with what confidence, what a proposed change must contain before a customer merges it, what evidence proves it worked, and what the system remembers for the next cycle.
  • Define the autonomy ladder and its limits, from suggestion, to draft, to auto-opened pull request, to auto-rollout, along with the controls, defaults, and audit trail customers need to rely on it. Some rungs stay off by design, and you own those decisions.
  • Set the quality bar for a product that is non-deterministic: build the evaluation sets with engineering, decide what "good enough to ship" means, and hold that bar when it moves a date.
  • Recruit the first design partners yourself, sit in their triage rotations, turn what you learn there into the roadmap, and keep talking to them after launch.
  • Develop and defend the sizing, impact, and cost-to-serve analysis that engineering leadership and pricing partners need to make resourcing calls, partnering with engineering on the unit economics of inference and the data platform and bringing that cost profile into packaging, metering, and pricing before launch rather than after.
  • Deliver concise written and verbal communication to executive, engineering, and customer audiences, clarifying complex architecture, quality trade-offs, and go-to-market, including where agentic observability, product analytics, and experimentation are heading and how that shapes the product.

Who You Are:

  • You have shipped AI products, not prototypes: you have taken at least one AI-native product to production customers, and you can describe what it got wrong in the field and what you changed in response.
  • You treat evaluation as product work: you have built or commissioned evaluation sets, set the bar for shipping a model or prompt change, and held that bar under schedule pressure.
  • You are fluent in agent failure modes and design for non-determinism deliberately, accounting for confidence, reversibility, blast radius, review surfaces, and graceful failure.
  • You have a zero-to-one track record: you have started something with no roadmap and no team and got it to customers who renewed, you narrow ruthlessly, and you have ended a direction you championed and can explain why.
  • You read across staff engineers, consuming product teams, sales and FinOps, marketing, and finance, and turn diffuse signals into a defensible product position.
  • You are collaborative, opinionated, and comfortable with ambiguity: you build trust quickly with engineers, PM peers, designers, and commercial partners, you bring strong product opinions and adapt as new evidence emerges, and you write the document that gives diffuse work a shape.
  • You have 8+ years of Product Management experience, or a track record showing Staff-level capabilities in related software roles. We weigh shipped AI products and zero-to-one evidence more heavily than years.
  • You have a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience (preferred).

title: Field Enablement Manager (EMEA)
descriptionHtml:
The Team

Our GTM Enablement team plays a critical role in helping Datadog's Sales and Customer Success teams succeed by equipping them with the right skills, knowledge, and tools at the right time. We partner closely with teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Curriculum, and Operations to ensure enablement programs translate into real performance in the field.

If you like adding value and seeing the direct impact of your work, and you thrive in dynamic environments where you can roll up your sleeves and get things done, this role is for you.

The Opportunity

Datadog's Enterprise business across EMEA continues to scale, and we're looking for a Field Enablement Manager to deliver ongoing ramp and everboarding enablement for Enterprise sellers across key EMEA markets (including the UK, DACH, France, Benelux, and the Nordics) — ensuring global enablement programs land effectively amid complex, multi-country Enterprise deals.

You'll serve as a trusted partner to Enterprise Sales leaders, adapting global programs to the realities of the EMEA Enterprise motion — longer sales cycles, multi-stakeholder buying committees, and a diverse regional footprint — while staying tightly aligned with our global Field Enablement organization.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives operating independently, builds strong relationships in the field, and enjoys adapting enablement programs to meet the needs of a fast-growing, sophisticated Enterprise segment.

What You'll Do

  • Deliver live and virtual enablement sessions and implement training programs focused on ongoing ramp and everboarding that improve the performance and productivity of Enterprise sellers and leaders across EMEA.
  • Administer program certifications — score and evaluate submissions against established rubrics and provide structured feedback.
  • Conduct ongoing field listening (shadows, 1:1s, syncs with first-line leaders) to maintain a strong pulse on Enterprise business needs, gaps, and strengths across EMEA markets; share insights with the broader enablement team to shape programs and priorities.
  • Lead reinforcement and coaching to drive post-program adoption, including designing activities (role plays, deal clinics, skill practice sessions) that connect training to measurable behavior change in real, complex customer scenarios.
  • Partner with Curriculum, Program Management, and Operations to share field insights and pilot or co-build content, and work closely with first-line Enterprise Sales leaders to build trusted relationships, diagnose challenges, and deliver ad hoc training in response to emerging needs.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate delivery and reinforcement — including synthesizing field feedback and surfacing patterns — and model effective AI use for the teams you train.

Who You Are

  • 4–5 years of experience in sales enablement, field enablement, training, or a related GTM role, with a proven delivery track record supporting Enterprise Sales and/or Customer Success teams in a SaaS or technology environment; multi-country EMEA experience is a strong plus.
  • Strong understanding of Datadog and/or the broader technology industry, including foundational knowledge of Datadog's core product pillars (Infrastructure, APM, Logs) and the ability to connect product capabilities to Enterprise customer value.
  • Strong facilitator with experience delivering engaging live and virtual training sessions to senior, sophisticated audiences, and familiarity with Enterprise sales methodologies/frameworks such as MEDDICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, Sandler, etc. (certification a plus).
  • Solid business acumen and comfort using performance data, field feedback, and qualitative insights to inform enablement decisions; experience with Asana or similar project management tools is a plus.
  • Highly collaborative and relationship-oriented — you build trust quickly with sellers, managers, and cross-functional partners.
  • Organized, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently across a large, diverse region.
  • Fluent in English, with proficiency in one or more additional European languages a plus; willing and able to travel approximately 25% across EMEA.

Why This Role Matters

As a Field Enablement Manager supporting Datadog's EMEA Enterprise business, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring our global enablement programs translate into local impact for some of our most strategic sellers and customers. You'll help accelerate ramp, build seller confidence, and enable Enterprise teams to succeed with customers across one of Datadog's fastest-growing and most complex regions.

title: Office Operations Associate
descriptionHtml:
At Datadog, Office Operations run the day-to-day operations for Datadog and help to keep our employees safe, happy and productive, which means every day is different.  Office Operations work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog keeps scaling smoothly and remains a great place to work.

You’ll help keep our employees safe, happy and productive, which could mean ensuring we’re not running out of espresso beans and pretzels, planning an event for 80 people, or hosting a 50 guest meetup into our Sydney office - every day will be different.

descriptionHtml:
The Compliance Specialist, EMEA is a subject matter expert who owns employment, labor, and statutory compliance across the region (primarily France, Spain, Portugal, Netherlands, Ireland and UK). This is an individual-contributor role where you will be the region's go-to authority on People compliance, partnering closely with People Operations, Legal, People Business Partners and regional stakeholders to build and maintain compliant people processes that enable Datadog's continued growth in EMEA.

You'll join a growing team - currently a Compliance Coordinator and an incoming Apprentice joining in September - and will work closely with them, bringing a more experienced, hands-on perspective to help scale the team's compliance capabilities across the region.

descriptionHtml:

This role is centered on defining what content we create, where it lives, and how it drives discovery across both traditional search engines and emerging AI/LLM platforms.
